articles.title: In WWII, one Scottish island became a secret British bioweapon site and stayed toxic for nearly 50 years; now it's safe to visit
articles.summary: For decades, Gruinard Island was a place most people were better off avoiding.
articles.body: For decades, Gruinard Island was a place most people were better off avoiding. The small, uninhabited island off Scotland's north-west coast had acquired an unusual reputation during and after the Second World War, when stories circulated locally about dead animals, strange military activity and something dangerous left behind. The government eventually put up warning signs and kept people away. What had happened there was not fully understood by the public for years. Gruinard had been used for secret experiments involving anthrax, part of a British wartime effort to investigate biological weapons. The contamination proved remarkably persistent, leaving the island under quarantine for almost half a century before it was officially declared safe in 1990.How an isolated Scottish island became a biological weapons test siteGruinard lies in the waters of the north-west Highlands, separated from the mainland by a stretch of sea. Before the war, it was largely uninhabited and used for grazing. Its isolation made it suitable for military experiments that could not safely be carried out close to towns and populated areas.As reported by the BBC, in 1942, the British government acquired the 522-acre island and restricted access. The work was linked to Porton Down, the military research establishment in Wiltshire, where scientists were studying chemical and biological agents. Britain was looking at ways biological weapons might be used during the conflict with Nazi Germany.The project became known as Operation Vegetarian. Its proposed use of anthrax was tied to Germany's food supply. The idea involved contaminating cattle feed with anthrax spores so that livestock would become infected. Meat from infected animals could then spread the disease to people who consumed it.Sheep trials showed how far the anthrax weapon could spreadGruinard provided an open landscape in which those questions could be tested. Livestock were taken to the island and positioned at different distances from the planned releases. The experiments involved detonating devices that dispersed anthrax spores. Sheep exposed to the resulting clouds became ill and died. Their bodies were then dealt with on the island, including burial and incineration, in an attempt to contain the contamination.The work continued into 1943. By then, the tests had provided the military with evidence that anthrax could be used in the way scientists had feared. Millions of contaminated linseed cakes were subsequently produced as part of the wider Operation Vegetarian programme.The plan was never carried out against Germany. As the course of the war changed, including the Allied invasion of Normandy, the proposed attack was abandoned. The contaminated cakes were eventually destroyed.Why Gruinard became known as Scotland’s island of deathThe researchers left Gruinard, but the island did not simply return to normal. Anthrax spores can survive in soil for long periods, and the experimental area remained contaminated after the wartime work ended. There were reports of animals dying on the mainland near Gruinard Bay in the months after the experiments. The British government paid compensation to some affected people, while the public explanation for the deaths attributed them to a diseased sheep that had supposedly fallen from a passing ship.For local residents, the secrecy surrounding the island only added to the uncertainty. Access remained prohibited and warning signs were placed around the site. Gruinard became known locally as the island of death or the mystery island.As per the BBC, reporter Fyfe Robertson visited the area in 1962, he found that the military still regarded the island as too dangerous for ordinary visitors. The broadcast brought wider attention to the rumours surrounding the site, although much of the wartime story remained classified.A 1971 test revealed anthrax was still buried beneath GruinardKeeping people away was easier than removing the contamination. Early attempts to make Gruinard safe included chemical treatment and controlled burning, but these measures did not eliminate the problem.Tests carried out in 1971 found that anthrax was no longer detected on the surface but remained present deeper in the soil. That meant the risk had not disappeared. Disturbing the ground could potentially expose contaminated material again.The issue eventually drew the attention of campaigners. In 1981, members of the Dark Harvest Commandos travelled to Gruinard, collected soil samples and delivered some of the material to the area around Porton Down. The action was intended to draw attention to the continuing contamination and put pressure on the government to resolve it.A more extensive clean-up followed in the mid-1980s. Scientists treated the island with a mixture containing seawater and formaldehyde and removed contaminated soil from parts of the site for incineration.Gruinard was declared safe in 1990As reported by the BBC, on 24 April 1990, almost 48 years after the wartime experiments began, the British government announced that Gruinard Island was free of anthrax contamination. The declaration ended one of the longest-running environmental consequences of Britain's wartime biological weapons research. The island had spent nearly five decades under restrictions because of experiments that had taken place there during the Second World War.The episode also formed part of a much wider British biological weapons programme. Gruinard was the first site used for this type of testing, but it was not the only location associated with Britain's wartime biological warfare research.Britain later ended its offensive chemical and biological weapons programmes and ratified the Biological Weapons Convention in 1975, which prohibits the development, production and stockpiling of biological weapons.Gruinard’s wartime legacy outlasted the experiments that caused itThe old warning signs and the island's wartime reputation have given Gruinard an unusual place in Scottish history. What was once a restricted military testing ground is now accessible as part of the wider landscape of the north-west Highlands.Its history has also made the island a point of interest for visitors exploring the region. The landscape itself can appear unremarkable, which makes its wartime past easy to miss. There are no obvious remains of a battlefield or large industrial complex to explain why the island spent so long behind a quarantine barrier.The significance lies beneath the surface, both literally and historically. For much of the second half of the 20th Century, Gruinard was a reminder that the consequences of military research could persist long after an experiment had ended.You use AI every day. Anita Blanchard told authorities that she and her husband, who is Gypsy Rose Blanchard's half-brother, went to the 34-year-old's home and spotted Urker lying unconscious from an outside window, according to an incident report. A man accompanying Anita Blanchard and her husband then entered the house through a window and found Urker, who was not breathing and cold to the touch, according to the report. GYPSY ROSE BLANCHARD IS ENGAGED TO MAN WHO CONTACTED HER IN PRISON, REPORT SAYS Investigators recovered syringes and a spoon next to a brown powdery substance in the bathroom, as well as a handgun, two shot glasses, and a syringe on a nightstand next to the bed, the report states. After Urker failed to show up for work the following day, Anita Blanchard and Urker's employer decided to check on him, ultimately prompting them to contact law enforcement. articles.title: Two Iranian nationals charged over alleged terrorism plot targeting Jewish community in England
articles.summary: British police said Friday that they had charged two Iranian nationals accused of plotting a terrorist attack against the Jewish community in Manchester on the eve of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.
articles.body: British police said Friday that they had charged two Iranian nationals accused of plotting a terrorist attack against the Jewish community in Manchester on the eve of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar. Rahman Salehi, 34, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, were charged with “engaging in conduct in preparation for terrorist acts” on or before September 20, according to a British police statement. The two men had allegedly been in contact with an overseas third-party who might be in Iran in relation to the plot, the Metropolitan Police said. Salehi and Ahmadyan had components for manufacturing an improvised explosive device and conducted reconnaissance for potential targets, according to the statement. On Monday, police arrested five British nationals in connection with a massive security operation near a base used by the U.S. Air Force to facilitate strikes on Iran, the counterterrorism officials running the operation said. The five men, all from London and in their early to mid-20s, were arrested Sunday on suspicion of terrorism and explosives offenses after three suspicious vehicles were seen moving toward RAF Fairford, a Royal Air Force station about 90 minutes west of London. The men were released on bail, but police arrested a dual U.K.-Iranian national Thursday in relation to the incident. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Wednesday there are strong indications that Tehran played a part in the security incident outside the air base. Iran has denied any involvement. Vicki Evans, the senior national coordinator for counterterrorism policing, said the alleged plot in Manchester was not linked to the incident at the airbase. “This week also brought into sharp focus some of the wider threats being projected into the UK from Iran,” Evans said in the statement. “While this incident and the investigation into the RAF Fairford incident are not connected in any way, I want to reassure the public that CTP, working with our national security partners, are using the full range of our capabilities to protect the UK from any hostile acts.”

articles.title: Two men charged with terrorism offences in Manchester
articles.summary: The pair were arrested in the Northern Quarter area of the city on the eve of Yom Kippur.
articles.body:
Two Iranian nationals who arrived in the UK by small boat have been charged with terror offences over an alleged plot to target the Jewish community in Manchester.

Rahman Salehi, 35, of Salford, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, from Liverpool, are accused of preparing to commit an act of terrorism or assisting another to commit an act of terrorism on or before 20 September.

The men were arrested in Manchester's Northern Quarter on the eve of Yom Kippur, considered the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said news that two Iranian men had been charged over the alleged plot would be "deeply distressing" to Manchester's Jewish community, as the city marks one year since the Heaton Park Synagogue attack.

Counter Terrorism Police (CTP) allege the two men were in contact with a third-party overseas, who may be in Iran, in relation to the plot.

According to CTP, the men are accused of obtaining instructions to make a chlorine bomb, acquiring liquids, components and equipment for such a device, researching potential targets and conducting reconnaissance of potential locations for attack.

It is understood the suspects arrived via small boat in 2020 and 2023. One was granted asylum, and the other has a live asylum claim.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said: "These recent events are a stark reminder of the threats posed against this country from both terrorists and foreign state actors.

"Two suspects have been charged with planning a terrorist attack against Jewish communities in Manchester.

"This news will be deeply distressing for our Jewish communities, coming so soon after Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur.

"I know this will be especially true in Manchester, as we mark one year since the terrorist attack at Heaton Park Synagogue.

"The fact both suspects arrived by small boat several years ago is a reminder of the importance of our relentless work to tackle illegal migration into this country. While numbers are down, I know there is more we must do.

"It would be inappropriate to comment further on this case. But I can say that we will be unrelenting in our efforts to protect our Jewish communities, root out antisemitism in this country, and maintain our border security."

As part of the investigation, searches were carried out at addresses in Epworth Street, Liverpool, and Lancaster Road, Salford.

Greater Manchester Police's Deputy Chief Constable, Terry Woods, said: "We know this is particularly acute on the calendar anniversary of last year's terrorist atrocity at the Heaton Park synagogue, and during the Jewish High Holy days.

"Our ongoing and robust policing plans within the Jewish communities will endure, and the public can expect to see continued visibility with officers providing engagement and security."

The men are due to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Saturday.

articles.title: Paris Pont Neuf cave: How French street artist JR turned the oldest bridge in Paris into a giant walk-through art installation
articles.summary: The oldest bridge in Paris looks as though a mountain has swallowed it whole.
articles.body: The oldest bridge in Paris looks as though a mountain has swallowed it whole. French street artist JR, nicknamed the French Banksy, has covered the seventeenth-century Pont Neuf with La Caverne du Pont Neuf, an inflatable, walk-through cave stretching about 120 meters across the River Seine. Open free of charge from June 6 to June 28, 2026, the installation pays tribute to Christo and Jeanne-Claude, who wrapped the same bridge in fabric forty years earlier. Inside, visitors find towering rock-like arches and an immersive soundscape by Thomas Bangalter, formerly of Daft Punk, all designed to make Parisians stop and wonder.Why the oldest bridge in Paris suddenly looks like a mountain caveAccording to ArchDaily, the transformation began taking shape on May 21, when JR started inflating the artificial cave over a bridge that has carried Parisians across the Seine for more than 400 years. The structure is up to 18 meters high and built from 80 air-filled canvas arches, which were loaded from the river onto the bridge and unfurled between night and day.JR has said the idea is to bring mineral and nature back into the heart of the city. He also wanted people to do something unusual on the most famous bridge in Paris, stop walking and look around.Inside La Caverne du Pont Neuf: the inflatable arches, immersive sound, and scentVisitors enter through darkness and emerge into the light on the other side. JR described it as a journey each person can take in their own way. The sound design comes from Thomas Bangalter, who previously collaborated with JR at the Opéra Garnier. That earlier project, in 2023, made the Paris opera house appear to be a large cave.The experience also reaches beyond sight and sound. According to Designboom, scent becomes part of an installation by JR for the first time. Euronews reported that the project would include sound and augmented reality.A tribute to Christo and Jeanne-Claude forty years after The Pont Neuf WrappedAccording to AP News, the cave marks four decades since Christo and Jeanne-Claude covered the Pont Neuf in 40,000 square meters of champagne-colored fabric, drawing three million visitors. JR takes a very different approach. Instead of hiding the bridge under a smooth skin, he gives it a rugged, rocky identity, and the result blurs the line between landscape, architecture, and performance.Like the 1985 project, the cave received no public funding. JR paid for it through sales of his artwork and support from private partners. Entry was free, and the installation was open twenty-four hours a day after a weather-delayed start; it could also be seen from the riverbanks, nearby bridges, and passing boats. Boat operators on the Seine even offered cruises right beneath the artwork, with an unobstructed view of the whole installation. For those who wanted more, JR also showed preparatory sketches at Galerie Perrotin in the Marais through July 25.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: NBC Selected’s staff tested recovery shoes for a month from Hoka, Oofos, Kane, Nike and more to find the best ones. Plus, podiatrists’ share who should use them and when.
articles.body: There’s nothing better than taking off your shoes after wearing them for hours — actually there is: taking them off and putting on a pair of recovery shoes. Simply put, podiatrists say this specific type of footwear is designed to give your feet a break. They’re made with shock-absorbing materials that feel equal parts soft and supportive, allowing your feet to get rid of tension, aches and pains between activities. And when I say “activities,” I don’t just mean running, lifting weights, walking and playing sports — recovery shoes can benefit anyone on their feet all day who needs a little relief. To narrow down the absolute best recovery shoes on the market, the NBC Selected staff and I spent over a month testing almost 11 pairs to share our first-hand experiences with them. I also interviewed two podiatrists, gathering information about the most important features to look for while shopping and why you shouldn’t wear recovery shoes all day. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best recovery shoes, tested and reviewed The NBC Selected staff tested the recovery shoes below for over a month to share their hands-on experiences with them. Before I assigned each tester a shoe, I made sure it had features that align with podiatrists’ shopping advice, including contoured insoles, deep heel cups, balanced cushioning and effective traction on the outsoles. I also noted which shoes are water-resistant and earned the American Podiatric Medical Association’s Seal of Acceptance. Learn more about how to shop for recovery shoes here and how we tested our picks here. Best basic slides Oofos was one of the first brands to introduce the idea of recovery shoes, and over the years, it’s expanded its reach from runners to anyone looking to relieve fatigued feet, says Dr. Anne Sharkey, a podiatrist at the North Austin Foot and Ankle Institute. The OOahh Recovery Slide is one of the most well-known styles, and it’s also the first recovery shoe I tried. I’ve worn it ever since I trained for my first 10K over a decade ago — after seeing how much I love my slides, my dad even bought a pair to use after golf. When I put on the OOahh slides after a run, my swollen feet instantly breathe a sigh of relief. The insoles delicately cradle my arches, and the outsoles are semi-curved: They’re not totally flat, and they’re not severely rocker-shaped to the point that I have trouble balancing. The outsoles taper inward toward the middle of my feet, which the brand says forces them to stay centered on the base instead of sliding side to side — the textured insoles also help with this. I feel where the outsole gets narrower when I’m wearing the shoes, and while it’s not uncomfortable, the sensation took a little getting used to. These shoes are made with a medium-thick layer of cushioning that has a bit of give. However, it isn’t so soft that I sink into it. I also love that the straps have a cutout in the center, which lets air flow through and adds a bit of flexibility, securing my feet without restricting them. Best for the flip flop obsessed While the OOahh slide is arguably Oofos’ most popular recovery shoe, the brand’s first-ever style was the OOriginal sandal. These two shoes are nearly identical: they’re made from the same type of impact-absorbing material and have similar outsole shapes. The biggest difference is that the OOriginal Sandal has a toe post, so it’s a flip flop, not a slide. The sandal is also 0.4 oz. lighter than the slide, which, in my experience, isn’t noticeable. NBC Selected commerce editor Cory Fernandez says the toe post felt comfortable the whole time he wore these sandals, and that the material didn’t bother his skin. He also found the shoes to be well-constructed. “I appreciate that they don’t feel cheap, and they provide great arch support without it being painful the first time I wore them,” he says. “They have a somewhat bouncy feel to them, so I felt like I could walk for a while.” Best for someone who likes maximum cushioning In true Hoka fashion, the Ora recovery slides are one of the most highly cushioned pairs I tested with a substantial rocker-shaped outsole — they lift me off the ground more than most other options on this list, and they help me roll through strides so I’m noticeably using less energy to walk post-activity. Thanks to the wider base and medium-soft foam, my feet and ankles are surprisingly stable while I’m moving and standing still. The shoe is also very solid — it’s as far away from a flimsy sandal as it could get, and the support is obvious as soon as I slip my feet inside. These recovery shoes have four cutouts on the straps to allow for lots of airflow, and their textured outsoles have a lug-shaped design for maximum traction. NBC Selected editorial director (and three-time marathoner) Lauren Swanson swears by them. “I’ve worn Hoka’s recovery slides for years — pretty much since I started running long distances,” she says. “After a long run, my feet swell enough that most shoes feel like punishment; these are the only things I want to put on.” Best clog (and biggest fashion statement) I’m not exaggerating when I say that I see multiple people wearing the Kane Revive in New York City every day, so I feel confident naming them one of the “it” shoes right now. They were one of two recovery shoes our team tested that are a clog style: They fully surround the feet, have a marginally curved outsole and are made with firmer cushioning, so we determined that they’re a sturdy recovery shoe that really locks feet in place, giving you extra support while walking. “Overall, the material is durable and the quality is great,” says NBC Selected senior editor Nikki Brown. She added that when she put these shoes on, she had to bend down to get the back of her feet inside using the built-in heel loop, so they’re pull-ons more than they are slip-ons. One of the most unique parts of this shoe is that its upper (the part covering the top of your feet) is perforated, which increases airflow. Our testers liked the breathability, but found that the material made noise when they were barefoot. There’s also raised nodes on the insoles that activate blood flow in key pressure points, according to the brand — it feels good apart from some minor tickling, says NBC Selected video producer Josh Rios. Because of these factors, Brown and Rios say wearing socks with the Revive OB is a must. Best for slipping on while hiding your toes If you like the look and sturdiness of the Kane Revive but want a true slip-on shoe, try the Kane Revive OB — “OB” stands for open-back, referring to the mule style of these shoes. Because you can shove your feet in these in seconds, they’re the more convenient option. And while there’s a larger heel cup to help keep your feet in place in the back, the Revive OB doesn’t feel as stable or secure as the standard Revive — they’re similar to any slide or flip flip, according to our testers. Regardless, Rios says wearing the Revive OB at home made his feet feel much more relaxed, and he used socks with them since they have the raised nodes on the insoles like the original Revive. Best Crocs that aren’t actually “Crocs” Crocs is known for comfortable shoes that make you say “I don’t want to take these off,” which was our general takeaway after testing the brand’s Mellow Recovery Slide. It’s made with foam that’s just soft enough for your feet to relax into, while also giving you firmer support as needed. “I feel like these shoes have molded to my feet over time, but they still maintain their shape and sturdiness,” says Brown. She has flat feet and finds it painful to walk barefoot on her apartment’s hardwood floors, so she keeps them next to her bed and outside the shower to slip on immediately. She uses them after exercising, be it a dumbbell workout, power walk or light jog. Brown says these slides have a snug fit, but they never felt tight, and that the material didn’t cause blistering or sensitivity. Because of that, she happily wore them with and without socks, which she didn’t experience with the other shoe she tested. The slides’ straps have breathability windows for extra airflow, and their outsole is on the flatter side, which made me feel balanced while standing and walking. Best for year-round wear Similar to the Kane Revive, these Nike recovery shoes are a clog style, so they cover the whole foot and you pull them on your feet, making them feel secure while you’re walking. They have perforations that allow for airflow, but only on the top of the shoe rather than across all parts of it — this makes them less breathable than the Kane Revives, so in hot temperatures, your feet might feel sweaty, says NBC Selected associate social media editor Caitlin Cusack. To avoid that, she paired them with socks and was comfortable for hours. “My feet always felt supported and cushioned while wearing these,” says Cusack. “Especially after a long workout or walk, it felt nice to have something so soft under my feet.” She added that the shoe’s material is durable and feels high quality — she didn’t notice any visible wear and tear during the testing period and can tell that they’ll last a long time. One of the biggest benefits of having fewer perforations on the Nike ReactX Rejuven8 shoes is that it makes them better for year-round wear — you can add thicker socks to keep your feet cozy in the fall and winter, and thinner socks in the spring and summer. Since you’ll likely want to add socks, Cusack recommends sizing up in these shoes. Best for frequently swollen feet Vionic’s recovery sandal has one of the deepest (if not the deepest) heel cups out of all the pairs we tested, making its side walls higher toward the middle — together, these features stabilize your feet and encourage them to stay in a position that aligns them with the ankles, according to the brand. The slides are designed with highly contoured insoles to maximize arch support, and cushioning that makes them feel firm with a little bit of cushiness and bounce, according to NBC Selected associate SEO reporter Ashley Morris. There’s also tons of traction thanks to the lugged outsoles. One of Morris’ favorite parts of these slides is the adjustable strap. It lets her customize how tight or loose she wants it to feel across her feet depending on how swollen they are post-activity. Depending on which option you buy, the strap is made from either suede or synthetic nubuck, which gives it a more stylish rather than sporty look and makes it feel soft against Morris’ skin. One important note: Vionic’s slides have a taller platform, which is not ideal for those with balance issues. Best for someone who suffers in heels all day As someone who often wears heels for hours, NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans is a prime candidate for recovery shoes. But she didn’t know how much she needed them until trying Kuru’s. “My feet kind of just relax as soon as I slide them on, and I feel all the tension in my legs and thighs come down and then disappear,” says Evans. “They have a thick heel with cushioning that feels just right — it’s not too soft and it’s not hard.” Evans mainly keeps her recovery slides at the office, giving her something to change into when her feet decide they’re done with heels. She loves the adjustable strap on Kuru’s Moment Recovery Slides, which lets her make them tighter or looser depending on how swollen her feet are at any given moment. The slides also have a built-in orthotic insole and targeted cushioning that cradles the heels to boost ankle stability and arch support, according to the brand. Best design specifically for women’s feet NBC Selected commerce editor Mili Godio reached for Fitflop’s slides after exercising and spending long days in heels at the office. She says her feet felt great resting on them for a few hours, and because they’re not bulky looking, she could pair them with casual outfits and look cute. The slides are firmer overall, making them very sturdy, but the footbed is semi-flexible, so they’re not too stiff. They also have three types of cushioning to align with what type of support each stage of a step needs, promoting natural movement, absorbing impact and conserving your energy, according to the brand: The cushioning is firmer around the heel, soft in the middle and medium-soft by the toes. Godio immediately noticed these slides’ arch support when she wore them for the first time, and she finds it effective as someone with high arches. She only has one drawback: Fitflop says these slides have a wider fit, but Godio, who has wide feet, experienced some rubbing underneath the ventilated straps. That said, she still comfortably wore the slides, so it wasn’t terribly noticeable. Most stable, grounded feel Almost everything about Nobull’s Recharge Slides remind me of Crocs’ Mellow Slides. Their overall look, shape and feel are comparable: They both have a moderate layer of semi-soft cushioning with a flatter outsole, making me feel comfortable, stable and grounded while wearing them. They’re also each designed with a textured insole to help feet stay in place. The biggest difference is that unlike the Crocs Mellows, Nobulls’ slides don’t have cutouts on the straps, so there’s no airflow around that part of my foot. The strap rests on top of my foot to keep it secure, but overtime, it gets hot against my skin, and the rubbing has led to chaffing, in my experience, especially since my foot is on the wider side. To prevent irritation, I only wear these slides with socks — I don’t mind, but I would like the option of wearing them without socks similar to how I can with other recovery slides I tested. How to shop for recovery shoes Before we tested recovery shoes, I talked to two podiatrists about the most important factors to consider while shopping for and evaluating them. Here’s what they recommend. APMA Seal of Acceptance: Brands can pay a fee and submit their recovery shoes to get independently evaluated by the American Podiatric Medical Association. If shoes meet specific safety and quality criteria, the third-party organization deems them to promote good foot health and gives them the APMA Seal of Acceptance, which is the gold standard in the shoe world, experts told me. That doesn’t mean shoes that don’t have the seal are ineffective — most likely, the brand just didn’t opt into the evaluation process yet.Cushioning: “Well-designed recovery shoes are constructed with materials that remove shock from the joints,” says Sharkey. “But softer doesn’t equal better. If the shoe feels like a marshmallow and your feet sink into the cushioning, it’s not giving you stability. A true recovery shoe is going to be cushioned plus supportive and stabilizing.”Insole and heel cup: The recovery shoe’s insole should be contoured, not flat, and the heel area should be somewhat sunken in to hug the back of your foot (this is technically called a deep heel cup), says Sharkey. These features add support and help the shoes stay on your feet. Your foot shape and arch type determine whether you find a shoe’s contoured footbed and heel cup comfortable, so it may take a trial-and-error to find a pair that feels like it’s tailored to your feet — it shouldn’t feel like the insole and heel cup are forcing them into a position they don’t want to be in, says Sharkey.Base shape: The base of the shoe should be wide enough to accommodate the width of your feet, says Sharkey. Make sure your feet aren’t hanging off the sides or spilling over the back or front. The base should also add stability. Many recovery shoes have a curved, rocker-shaped base, which helps propel you forward while walking. It also helps take stress off the metatarsals, which are the long bones in the ball of your foot — the curved base transfers pressure away from this area and reduces motion in the toe joints, says Dr. Bobby Pourziaee, a podiatrist at Rodeo Drive Podiatry.. Some people have no problem walking in a shoe with a rocker-shaped base, but others find it destabilizing and should choose a recovery shoe with a flat base instead.Grip: Your recovery shoes should have enough grip on the outsoles to give you traction on indoor and outdoor surfaces, says Sharkey. You shouldn’t feel like you’re slipping and sliding while walking in them. Fit: Recovery shoes come as slides, flip flops, mules and clogs. The style you choose is a personal preference — fit is the most important thing to pay attention to. Too much room around your feet might cause you to grip the insoles with your toes to keep the shoes on while you walk, which can lead to toe, foot and leg strain, says Sharkey. On the other hand, not enough room around your feet might cause chafing, blisters and pain. When evaluating fit, make sure your feet rest comfortably in the shoes while standing and walking so you can get the full recovery benefits.Water resistance: Buying recovery shoes made from a water-resistant material lets you wear them outside regardless of weather conditions, and in the shower while you’re in public places like locker rooms and hotels, says Sharkey. How we tested recovery shoes Our methodology Before the NBC Selected staff tested recovery shoes, I talked to two podiatrists about them to learn what they are, how they work, how to appropriately wear them and what factors to pay attention to while shopping for and evaluating them. I also asked experts about the most popular brands on the market. I researched each one they mentioned and made a list of 11 recovery shoes from nine brands that are highly-rated among customers and experts for the NBC Selected staff to test. I noted which ones earned the APMA Seal of Acceptance. Brands sent us the recovery shoes as courtesy samples. Up to two people tested each recovery shoe on our list for over a month and evaluated them according to the criteria I detail below. Testers submitted their feedback via a form, and I reviewed the results to compile our comprehensive list of recommendations. Recovery shoe testing criteria Cushioning: Experts say that ideally, recovery shoes’ cushioning feels soft enough to relieve foot tension, but firm enough to avoid sinking into it. Testers noted how close their shoes got to this description.Insole and heel cup: Testers described how contoured, if at all, their shoes’ insoles were, and how prominent of a deep heel cup their shoes had. They shared how supportive and comfortable they found the insole and heel cup, and shared details about their foot shape and arch type to contextualize their feedback.Base shape: We tested recovery shoes with flat and rocker-shaped outsoles, as well as those that land somewhere in between. Testers described the shape of their shoes’ outsole and how stable it made them feel while walking and standing. They also shared information about their foot size and width to contextualize how well their feet fit on their shoes’ base.Grip: Testers looked at the bottom of their recovery shoes to see what it looked like, identifying any texture or other components that added grip. They paid attention to how much traction the outsoles gave them on various indoor and outdoor surfaces (including in different weather conditions) to prevent slipping and sliding.Fit and feel: Each tester used the size charts on brands’ websites to choose the appropriate size recovery shoe for their feet. We assessed whether each shoe was true-to-size and how they accommodated the shape, width and length of our feet. If the shoes did not fit well, testers specified areas that were too roomy, tight, narrow, wide, short or long.Style: We tested recovery slides, mules and clogs, noting the benefits and drawbacks of each style to make comparisons.Activity: Per experts’ recommendations, testers wore their recovery shoes directly after physical activity, after being on their feet for hours and at home to avoid going barefoot. They walked and stood in them, and wore them inside and outside. Testers regularly wore their recovery shoes for over a month before submitting feedback about them.Durability: After a month of testing, we evaluated how much visible wear and tear we saw on our recovery shoes, and whether their fit, comfort level and support level changed at all with consistent use.Cleaning and maintenance: Testers cared for their recovery shoes as recommended by the brand, which could involve machine-washing or hand-washing, and air drying. After cleaning their recovery shoes, testers described any changes they noticed, especially in regard to fit, look and material quality. Meet our podiatry experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also ensure that all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and with no undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Dr. Anne Sharkey is a podiatrist at the North Austin Foot and Ankle Institute.Dr. Bobby Pourziaee is a podiatrist at Rodeo Drive Podiatry. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a reporter at NBC Selected who has covered footwear for over six years. For example, I’ve written about running sneakers, walking sneakers, running sneakers with arch support and sneakers for plantar fasciitis. I also try dozens of shoes from various brands each year. To write this article, I talked to two podiatrists about recovery shoes, how to appropriately wear them and what to consider while shopping for and evaluating them. I also researched the most popular recovery shoes, requested courtesy samples from brands and coordinated a month of testing among the NBC Selected staff so we could share our first-hand experiences with them. As a long-distance runner, I’ve worn recovery shoes for years and have in-depth knowledge about their benefits. Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok to stay up to date.

articles.title: Hawaii's iconic 500-year-old Hōlei Sea Arch has collapsed into the sea
articles.summary: The lava rock formation protruding from the rocky cliffs of Volcanoes National Park crumbled some time last weekend.
articles.body:
Hawaii's famous Hōlei Sea Arch, a 90-foot-tall (27.4m) lava rock structure that formed about 550 years ago, has collapsed into the Pacific Ocean.

The collapse's exact time is not known. The arch was still projecting into the water from the coast of Volcanoes National Park on 23 September, but was gone by 27 September, the National Park Service (NPS) said.

"The coastline flanking the sea arch has shown signs of instability for years," NPS, which warned in 2021 that the arch would eventually crumble, said in a statement.

Located at the end of Chain of Craters Road on the island of Hawaii, also called "the big island", the formation was a popular - and heavily photographed - tourist destination.

The arch is believed to have fallen when the park was temporarily closed during Tropical Storm Nolo last weekend.

The park service said earthquakes during the 2018 Kīlauea volcano eruption and summit collapse had damaged the cliffs near the arch.

Its ultimate collapse marks "the latest transformation of the park's remote and rugged coastline".

In January 2020, new cracks and instability in the cliffs led the park to close the original arch viewing area, and a few months later, a new viewing area opened at a safer distance, NPS said.

Waves from a tropical storm later that year broke off a chunk of rock from the bottom of the arch.

"This formation is beautiful, but temporary, and has a limited life span," the park service said in 2021. "The sea arch will eventually crumble into the sea. However, others will replace it as the cliff slowly migrates inland."

Thousands of people have liked and commented on the NPS social media post about the arch's collapse, including sharing their memories of visiting the arch and posting photos of it.

"Nothing and no one is here forever," one Facebook user commented. "Millions of years from now the sun will die. Appreciate the good, the beauty, now."

articles.title: JUAN WILLIAMS: My wife thought I was crazy to join Fox News. I'm glad I did
articles.summary: Juan Williams reflects on leaving CNN to join Rupert Murdoch's startup Fox News Channel 30 years ago and the friendships that defined his career.
articles.body: My wife said I was crazy. This was 1996, thirty years ago. I worked for the established brand name in cable television, CNN. FOX NEWS CHANNEL TOPS NBC, ABC AND CBS IN KEY RATINGS MEASURABLE FOR SECOND STRAIGHT SUMMER Why then, she asked, with three young school-age children still at home, was I willing to give up that prime seat to join a start-up cable network being launched by a controversial Australian media mogul, Rupert Murdoch? And this start-up Fox News Channel faced an uphill fight just to get on cable systems in big cities, including New York. "Crazy!" Yes! But I told her they were going to be scrappy, innovative, and give me a foothold on the ground floor of the next era of news. So, I went with the new kids in cable news. And Fox delivered over the last 30 years by doing news for people who did not watch news. Fox is now often the number one channel of any kind on cable. From the early days, the screen has been full of colorful graphics. Stories come and go fast. Heroes and villains are clear-cut. Crime stories and war stories took center stage — no matter where they occurred. The on-air people did not speak down to the audience as experts. They talked to them as friends and neighbors, always shaking their heads at a crazy world. As Brit Hume, now Fox's chief political analyst, told me at the start, Fox was willing to do stories being ignored by the news networks and cable outlets. He said Fox News was picking up money others left on the street. DANA PERINO: THE UNTOLD STORY OF THE REMARKABLE PEOPLE WHO MAKE FOX NEWS POSSIBLE On top of being daring, Fox had the novel idea of featuring right-of-center voices, Republican political players who generally felt like outsiders on the other networks. Roger Ailes, the first head of the network, knew politics. He was a top GOP consultant. And his top programming aide, Chet Collier, a Democrat, had been Ailes' mentor at the popular daytime talk show, "The Mike Douglas Show." They sold me on Fox, and they knew exactly what they were getting with me. I'd worked at The Washington Post and CNN. In bestselling books, I called out politicians on the right and the left. And as a Black journalist, I was known to trade punches with Black politicians. Fox's founders wanted me to trade punches with their right-wing media personalities. I was happy to get in on the action. From the start, Fox made good television. Ratings slowly climbed as viewers discovered turn-up-the-volume debates among finger-pointing, smirking, laughing, and eye-rolling personalities. Fox was in the right place as bombshell revelations hit the air about the president of the United States having a sexual relationship with a White House intern. DR. MARC SIEGEL: WHAT 18 YEARS AT FOX TAUGHT ME ABOUT COURAGE AND FAITH The impeachment of a president included nightly stories about the popular President Clinton facing a hard-edged prosecutor, Kenneth Starr. And then came provocative reports about a blue dress and cigars. The ratings climbed. What I remember most about those early years of Fox is being on set in the D.C. bureau with Brit Hume, then the managing editor. He held the air for hours of hearings and press conferences. I was by his side as we struggled with new equipment, technicians discovering buttons, and producers shouting breaking news into our earpieces. I think about the amazing Fox audience — the countless people who treat me as a friend when we meet in diners, airports, supermarkets, campaign rallies, ball games, convention halls, studios and green rooms across America. The same chaos followed when "Fox News Sunday" hit the air. No studio was ready. So, Tony Snow, the show's first moderator, and Marty Ryan, the top producer, had to hunt for historic homes, even gardens, in Washington, D.C. For Snow, Hume, and an all-star panel of D.C. commentators, including Fred Barnes, Mort Kondracke — hail to the Beltway Boys — Mara Liasson, Bill Kristol, and Charles Krauthammer, every show was about speaking directly to the hot, populist passions in politics. It was about being sharp with each other and giving no quarter to political guests. Creating the best show for the people at home has remained the goal for Fox. Krauthammer would win laughs and applause on the lecture circuit by beginning his speeches by saying he was grateful to be invited anywhere Juan Williams could not interrupt him. By 2000, Fox was perfectly positioned to offer 24/7 news and analysis of the disputed presidential election, the Florida recount, and the 5–4 Supreme Court decision that gave the White House to an underdog Republican who lost the popular vote. And when terrorists struck the World Trade Center and the Pentagon on September 11, 2001 — 25 years ago this month — Fox was there with an established news-gathering operation and unique access to the new Republican administration of President George W. Bush. Then came Fox News' coverage of the war in Iraq and the fight against terrorist cells in Afghanistan. Fox's ratings grew as more and more viewers trusted that, no matter their politics, Fox delivered the most compelling take on the sizzling stories defining each election, especially the 2008 race that saw a little-known Black senator running against former First Lady Hillary Clinton for the Democratic nomination. GREGG JARRETT: MY MOTHER’S ADVICE LED ME TO THE CAREER OF A LIFETIME It was a freezing night in Des Moines when the "All-Star" panel realized Barack Obama, a Black man, was about to win the Iowa caucuses. On the air, I started crying. My emotion got to me as I tried to explain to the Fox audience what that moment meant to our nation's history, and especially to Black American history. Another memory is being lustily booed by an auditorium full of South Carolina Republican voters in 2012. The booing started when, while asking questions at a Fox-sponsored GOP primary debate, I questioned Newt Gingrich about his use of racially loaded rhetoric concerning President Obama and the poor. Years later, I would joke with the Speaker that he had me to thank for his upset victory in the Palmetto State primary. That exchange became one of the first viral moments of a presidential campaign in the early internet age. FOX NEWS DIGITAL LEADS IN UNIQUE VISITORS, OTHER KEY METRICS AGAINST CNN, NY TIMES DURING AUGUST By Obama's second term, I was spending more time in the New York studios as a co-host of "The Five." By 2015, I began nearly a decade of living in New York to co-host the show. My role was described by Ailes as a center-left foil to the conservatives on the show. Politico summed up my role this way: "Fox's Lone-Wolf Liberal Had a Tough Job. But It Made for Better TV." "Juan Williams was particularly good at what might be the hardest, least appreciated, and most important job in cable news," the outlet wrote. "The Five" became the number one show on the number one cable channel and delivered a robust message about debate in America. No matter your politics, no matter if you are with conservatives or liberals, and no matter racial and religious lines, "We the People" — Americans of all stripes — can find common ground in defense of honest debate, even with rants and occasional posturing. "You cut a path through the jungle," a friend recently told me as we reminisced about the state of the media and the dearth today of conservative media platforms where liberals feel comfortable appearing, as well as liberal platforms where conservatives feel comfortable appearing. I told him that since Fox became the number one cable news channel, it is often the case that more Democrats are watching Fox than any other cable news channel. I've written more than a dozen books over the last 30 years. And on book tours, hard-right conservatives show up to tell me they disagree with me but love hearing a different point of view from someone they trust and, sometimes grudgingly, even like. In truth, working with Brit, Shannon Bream, Bret Baier, Bill O'Reilly, Sean Hannity, and so many others almost always ended with more conversation, then dinner, a ballgame, or a beer. Brit once said the two of us are like TV's pro wrestlers. We fight like hell tonight, and the next night we go to another town and do it again. At its best, Fox News is a reminder that social media and the internet are not real life. The bitterness we see online is produced by computer algorithms designed to divide Americans. Fox is about the audience. There's a bond. That is why, on Fox News' 30th anniversary, I find myself thinking less about ratings or political fights than about friendships. I think about Charles. I think about Tony. I think about Roger and Chet. I think about Brit, Mara, Bill, Fred, Chris, and Bret. I think about people like Cherie Grzech, who directed politics, and Porter Berry, who ran shows before taking control of FoxNews.com. I think about former television producer Nate Fredman. I think about Lynne Jordal Martin, who edits for FoxNews.com. I shared offices with Mike Emanuel and Leland Vittert. I think about the amazing Fox audience — the countless people who treat me as a friend when we meet in diners, airports, supermarkets, campaign rallies, ball games, convention halls, studios, and green rooms across America. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION And I think about the people viewers rarely see: editors, producers, bookers, tech operators, directors, hair and makeup artists, security guards, and janitors. So, three cheers for Fox News — one for each decade we have been on the air. Thank you to the viewers and FoxNews.com readers who made our success possible. Thirty years ago, my wife thought I was crazy. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP She still thinks I am, and maybe she's right. But I'm awfully glad I took the chance. articles.title: Unsolicited advice to Supreme Court lands trial judge in trouble
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: It sounds inconceivable that a trial judge will advise the top court of the country on how to decide a case.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: It sounds inconceivable that a trial judge will advise the top court of the country on how to decide a case. But it happened recently, and the judge is now in trouble, with the Supreme Court seeking an explanation from him for advising it on when to grant bail.The case pertains to the bail petition of an accused from West Bengal who has been an undertrial prisoner for the last five years, and the apex court, while rejecting his plea, had asked the trial court to complete the proceedings within three months. The order, which was passed on May 11, directed the trial court to file a report after disposal of the case.As the trial court could not honour the SC order, the judge wrote to the apex court seeking more time to conclude the trial. But the judge, the additional district and sessions judge, 3rd court, North 24 Parganas at Barasat, also gave some unsolicited advice to the apex court on bail jurisprudence - when to grant bail and when not.After reading the letter, which was placed before a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran, the court expressed shock over its contents, which were uncalled for and directed its registry to ask the judge why he wrote what he wrote. The bench, however, did not reveal the exact wording of the letter but noted in its order that the judge conveyed words of advice."We are quite disturbed with the manner in which the trial judge has addressed a letter to this court requesting some more time. It is not for the presiding officer to convey words of advice as to when this court should grant bail and should not grant bail. The last two paragraphs of the letter are something which we have not appreciated. Registry to call for an appropriate explanation from the presiding officer at the earliest," SC said.The judge had written the letter dated Aug 11 addressed to the assistant registrar, Supreme Court, and prayed for some more time to complete the trial. Fixing the time for completion of the trial, SC in May had noted the case was proceeding at a snail's pace and asked that the trial be expedited as the accused had been languishing in jail for the last five years.Referring to a Calcutta HC order which had rejected the bail plea in March, saying all witnesses would be examined by the end of April, SC had said in its May order, "Although the HC was quite confident the remaining 12 witnesses would be examined by May 1, yet it seems not a single witness has been examined... We give one last chance to the state to proceed further with the recording of evidence of the remaining witnesses. articles.title: I found 14 Walmart fashion pieces that look straight off a designer runway — and they’re all under $100
articles.summary: I tested clothing and accessories at Walmart to find the best pieces under $100, including workwear, fall jackets, sneakers, boots and bags.
articles.body: Walmart has been making its way onto my timeline a lot lately for its fashion offerings, so I decided to see if the clothes actually live up to the hype. To give some context, I’m 24 years old and a recent grad paying New York City rent. Most, if not all, of my clothes are from Depop, Poshmark, or eBay. I occasionally buy newly made clothes, but I never saw Walmart as a fashion destination that I would consider for my fall wardrobe. To my surprise, the retailer has a large fashion portfolio, including exclusive brands like Scoop, Free Assembly, Scenario, Joyspun, Avia and Athletic Works, along with collaborations and collections from brands like Madden NYC, Levi’s, Hanes and Reebok. I’m someone who genuinely loves shopping for clothes, but I’m also always looking for pieces that feel stylish and well-made but don’t cost a small fortune. So, when I went to a Walmart Supercenter and spent hours browsing the racks and trying things on I was pleasantly surprised. I found workwear I could easily incorporate into my office wardrobe, jackets that reminded me of pieces I’ve seen at much more expensive retailers, comfortable shoes, everyday bags and plenty of basics. Most importantly, these weren’t pieces I liked for the price. Many of them were clothes and accessories I would genuinely wear regardless of where they came from and they were affordable. Below are my favorite Walmart fashion finds from my shopping trip, including pieces I bought or would go back for. Every piece costs less than $100. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best clothing from Walmart From a genuine suede jacket to $27 sneakers, these are the exclusive Walmart fashion finds that impressed me most after trying them in person. Best tops This was one of my favorite workwear finds. The lightweight fabric feels relaxed rather than stiff, and the tie detail gives you multiple ways to style it: I especially liked that I could tie it in the front or back depending on the look I wanted. I’m 5-foot-5 and typically wear a medium, but I comfortably fit a size a small, so you may want to consider sizing down depending on your preferred fit. It reminds me of blouses I own from J.Crew and Banana Republic (where I am a loyal credit card holder, respectively), but at a much lower price. My size wasn’t available in store, but this blouse immediately stood out as a business-casual staple. It has an intentionally flowy, oversized silhouette with voluminous bishop sleeves, and the cotton fabric makes it a practical layering piece as temperatures change. I’d pair it with fitted or tailored pants to balance the volume on top, but it would work equally well with jeans or a midi skirt. The first thing I noticed about this top was how soft it felt. It has a relaxed, oversized shape, drop shoulders and a three-button Henley neckline, making it something I could easily wear around the house as loungewear and then keep on to run errands. The fabric is lightweight, breathable and slightly stretchy, while the cuffed sleeves and curved hem make it look more put-together than your average pajama top. It would be the ideal top for traveling — though I once swore I would never show up to the airport in pjs. Best sweaters and jackets This was probably my favorite find of the entire trip. Although Walmart describes it as cropped, it didn’t feel particularly short on my 5-foot-5 frame, especially when I paired it with mid-waisted jeans. The removable matching scarf is what really sold me: wear it together for a preppy, country-club-inspired look or remove it when you want a simple crewneck. The sweater reminded me of some of the cashmere and knit styles I’ve seen at Gap, and I could easily wear it to work, school or on the weekend. Be a corporate baddie — but make it under $60. That’s the thought that immediately entered my mind when I saw myself in this blazer. The version I tried in store didn’t have the embellishments, but I loved the relaxed, boxy silhouette and especially liked wearing it open. It gave me the polished, slightly oversized look I associate with brands like Aritzia and Reformation. The online version comes with detachable jeweled pins on the lapel, which gives you even more ways to style it. Remove them for work, add them back for a more playful look or swap in your own brooches and accessories. At less than $15, this sweater vest one of the best values I found. The knit felt soft and didn’t shed while I was trying it on, and the colors looked just as rich and vibrant in person as it does online. The tailored edges and button front make it easy to layer over a blouse or T-shirt for work, but you can also wear it alone with jeans or a skirt. I’d size up if you want a more relaxed, oversized look. The styling reminded me of knitwear I’d typically look for at Zara or Mango. This jacket had so many little details that made it stand out. There’s a high collar, removable hood, cape-like yoke, pockets and an adjustable waist that lets you completely change the silhouette. I cinched mine to give the jacket more shape, and I loved how it looked and felt when I had it on. It reminded me of the playful utility outerwear I’ve seen from brands like Sandy Liang and Damson Madder, but without the designer price attached to it. This is the most expensive piece on my list, but it was also one of the biggest surprises. The jacket is made from 100% genuine suede and feels soft, warm and substantial. It has a cropped silhouette, stand collar, functional pockets and a full lining, and I immediately thought of jackets I’ve seen at vintage leather stores and retailers like Sézane and Revolve for considerably more. I even got compliments from other shoppers when I walked out of the dressing room wearing it. If I were going to splurge on one item from this list, this would be a contender. Best bags I picked up this bag while shopping and basically carried it around Walmart as if I already owned it. I love the slouchy hobo silhouette and woven-looking texture, which reminded me of much more expensive bags I’ve seen from Bottega Veneta and Anthropologie. It’s the type of bag I could see myself using every day because the shape makes a statement without being difficult to style. This was easily one of the cutest accessories I found. The bag has a soft faux suede body, faux leather trim and gold-tone hardware, but my favorite detail is the magnetic sides: you can wear it in the triangular silhouette or release them to create a more rectangular shape and give yourself additional room inside. I don’t see this silhouette often at mass retailers, which is part of what made it stand out to me. For under $20, it’s an easy and inexpensive way to make a simple outfit more interesting. This tote immediately reminded me of my over $100 Longchamp bag, both in how it looked and how practical it felt. It has a spacious main compartment, an exterior zippered pocket and two interior pockets, so there’s room to organize the essentials you need for work or school. The shoulder straps also make it easy to carry around for longer periods. I’d use this for school, errands or even as a lightweight everyday work bag. Best shoes These boots combine two things I prioritize when shopping for fall shoes: comfort and versatility. I found them comfortable while walking around the store, and the squoval toe gives your feet more room than many pointed styles. I’ve also had good experiences with Steve Madden shoes (they hold up well), so I was especially interested in trying the Madden NYC line. These are an easy way to get the look of a classic tall fall boot without spending hundreds. These were comfortable as soon as I put them on thanks to the memory foam insole and padded collar and tongue, and I loved the faux suede texture. The double laces are an unexpected detail that makes them look much more interesting than a standard sneaker, especially in the green color I tried. They reminded me of fashion sneakers I’ve seen from Miista and Adidas without looking like they were simply trying to copy a more expensive shoe. Stylish, comfortable and $27: there isn’t much more I could ask for in an everyday sneaker. The breathable mesh upper and lightweight sole make these suitable for walking, running errands or casual workouts, and they also have odor-reducing technology, according to the brand. The sporty silhouette reminded me of some of my New Balance and Asics sneakers, making these one of my favorite budget-friendly shoe finds from the trip. These boots immediately reminded me of styles I own or have seen from Frye and Vagabond. The streamlined silhouette and pointed oval toe make them look polished, while the block heel keeps them practical for everyday wear. I also loved the color in person because it felt a little more rich than a standard black boot. I’d wear these with straight-leg jeans for work or dress them up with a skirt or dress for going out. How I picked the best Walmart fashion To find the best Walmart clothes, shoes and accessories, I visited a Walmart Supercenter and spent several hours browsing the fashion department and trying on pieces that caught my attention. I looked across several Walmart brands, including Scoop, Free Assembly, Scenario, No Boundaries and Avia, as well as brands sold at Walmart like Madden NYC. Because I shop for clothes frequently, I have a good sense of what I typically get for my money at different retailers. As I tried things on, I considered how each item compared to similar pieces already in my wardrobe, including clothing and accessories from more expensive brands. I ultimately prioritized the following: Fit: I paid attention to how each piece fit my 5-foot-5 frame, whether the sizing felt accurate and whether I would recommend sizing up or down.Material and feel: I looked for fabrics that felt comfortable and substantial for the price, and avoided pieces that felt excessively thin, scratchy or prone to shedding.Construction: I considered details like lining, seams, hardware, pockets, closures and adjustable elements that made an item feel more functional or well-made.Comfort: For shoes and everyday clothing in particular, I considered whether I could realistically wear the item for several hours. I live in NYC and commute, so these pieces have to hold up to subway rides, uneven concrete sidewalks and unpredictable weather.Versatility: I prioritized pieces I could style multiple ways or wear in different settings, including the office, weekends, errands and nights out.Price: Everything I recommend costs less than $100, and I considered whether I thought the quality, design and functionality of each item justified the price.Style: Finally, I chose pieces I genuinely liked. Many reminded me of silhouettes, materials or trends I’ve seen from more expensive retailers, but I only included items I would personally buy or recommend to someone else. How to shop for clothes and accessories at Superstores Shopping for clothes at a superstore like Walmart can be overwhelming. Unlike a traditional clothing retailer, you may be browsing several in-house and third-party brands at once, and sizing, materials and overall quality can vary between them. Here are a few things I recommend doing to make the process easier. Don’t rely solely on the size on the tag. Sizing can vary significantly between brands and even between different styles from the same brand. I typically wear a medium, for example, but comfortably fit into a small in some of the pieces I tried. If you’re shopping in person, I recommend bringing at least two sizes of anything you really like into the fitting room. Pay attention to the fabric and construction. One of the easiest ways to narrow down a crowded rack is to touch the clothes. I looked for fabrics that felt substantial, soft or comfortable and checked details like seams, lining, buttons, zippers and hardware. I also gently rubbed or handled knitwear to see whether it shed immediately. Check the material composition. Look at the tag or online product description before buying. The material can help you understand what you’re actually getting for the price. This was especially important with the Scoop Cropped Suede Jacket: I initially liked it because of how it looked and felt, but finding out that it was made from genuine suede made the $99 price more compelling to me. This will also be important when you consider things that can’t be machine washed — if you’re not going to ever hand wash or dry clean your clothes, you don’t want to end up with pieces that require this. Think about what you already own. A low price doesn’t necessarily make something a good purchase. Before buying, I ask myself what I would wear the item with and whether I can picture at least a few outfits using clothes I already own. Versatile pieces like sweaters, blazers, jackets and everyday bags may give you more opportunities to wear them. That being said, don’t purchase separates that you don’t already have matches for or you might end up with a closet full of cute tops and no bottoms to wear them with. Try unexpected brands and sections. Don’t limit yourself to one Walmart fashion brand just because you’ve had luck with it before. I found some of my favorite pieces across Scoop, Free Assembly, Scenario, No Boundaries and Avia, and each brand offered something different. Check online after browsing in the store. The selection at your local store may not represent everything Walmart carries. If you find something you like but can’t find your size or preferred color, check Walmart’s website or app. You may also find additional styles from the same brand that weren’t stocked at your location. Why trust NBC Selected? I am the editorial operations associate for NBC Selected where I work closely with our editors and reporters on shopping coverage and help coordinate large-scale product testing for franchises like our Wellness Awards and 100 Best series. I’m also an avid fashion shopper and regularly buy clothing and accessories across a range of price points and retailers. For this story, I visited a Walmart Supercenter and tried on clothing, shoes and accessories from several of its brands. I evaluated each item based on its fit, comfort, materials, construction, versatility and price, and only included pieces I would buy myself or recommend to others. articles.title: King's Caribbean tour will not shy away from 'darkest days of our past'
articles.summary: In recent years, the King has expressed his "personal sorrow" at the UK's role in slavery.
articles.body:
King Charles's upcoming Caribbean tour will not shy away from "the darkest days of our past", Buckingham Palace has said.

During the visits, the King is expected to face renewed calls to apologise for the UK's role in the transatlantic slave trade and be questioned on potential reparations - compensation from countries that took part in the slave trade.

The King and Queen Camilla are set to travel to Antigua and Barbuda for the Commonwealth Heads of Government meeting, with visits also to Bahamas and Guyana as part of the eight-day trip starting on October 27.

According to PA news agency, it is understood the government has not advised the King to apologise or offer reparations.

Jamaica to hand slavery reparations petition to King Charles

The King has previously expressed his "personal sorrow" at the UK's role in slavery.

A palace spokesperson said: "There are important discussions taking place in various fora about colonial legacy and the intergenerational impact of the transatlantic trade in enslaved persons.

"While these are primarily matters for Governments to address, His Majesty's previous statements on them have been unequivocal, describing them as an 'atrocity' which 'forever stains our history'."

The palace said the tour will "principally be oriented to the vibrant present and promising future of each country".

Several African and Caribbean countries have called for a formal apology and reparations from countries that benefited from the transatlantic slave trade.

In September, Jamaica's government said it would raise a petition on the subject of slavery reparations with the King, the country's head of state.

Olivia Grange, the country's culture minister, said the petition would ask the King to refer three questions to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council over the legality of the enslavement of Africans in Jamaica.

Last month, a Downing Street spokesperson said the transatlantic slave trade was "abhorrent" but the UK position was that it does not pay reparations.

articles.title: Tories pledge to build 50,000 new prison places
articles.summary: The party says its proposals would stop prisoners being released early and cut crime.
articles.body:
The Conservatives have promised to build 50,000 new prison places in England and Wales to stop criminals being released early, if they return to government.

The party said it would cost £2bn per year to build and run the new prisons, funded by spending cuts including to the foreign aid budget.

On Thursday hundreds of prisoners were released early , under new rules introduced to prevent jails reaching capacity, with around 4,500 due to be freed by next summer.

Labour blamed the previous Tory government for leaving "our criminal justice system at breaking point" and said the party's proposals were not "credible".

The announcement comes as Conservative members gather for the party's annual conference in Birmingham, which begins on Sunday.

Prisons in England and Wales have been running close to capacity for years, with the latest government figures showing they are 98% full.

Under the latest early release scheme, eligible prisoners can now be released on a community licence after serving one-third of their jail sentence.

Those excluded include prisoners convicted of murder, manslaughter, a sexual or grooming-related offence, or a driving offence that led to a death.

The government has also effectively scrapped one-year jail terms.

The Tories said they would use extra prison capacity to reverse these measures.

An early release programme introduced by the previous Conservative government saw more than 10,000 prisoners freed early between October 2023 and September 2024.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said: "A violent criminal doesn't become less dangerous just because the government has run out of prison cells."

She added: "[Labour's] answer is to let dangerous offenders out even earlier instead of building the prison spaces we need."

Labour Party chairwoman Bridget Phillipson said: "The Tories are taking the public for fools. Across 14 years in government, they added just 500 prison places and closed 23 prisons.

"Now Kemi Badenoch expects the British people to believe they'll build 50,000."

Meanwhile, the Prison Governors' Association said "long-term investment" was needed and warned a "staffing crisis" would pose challenges to delivering new prisons.

If the party wins power, the Tories said they would introduce legislation early in the new Parliament to override planning and procurement barriers, allowing the process to be "fast-tracked".

It said the use of private finance would help speed up delivery and control costs.

There are currently around 89,000 useable prison places in England and Wales, according to the latest government figures.

The Tories said their proposals would increase this figure by more than 50%, with the vast majority of new places expected within the party's first Parliament in government - up to five years - and the full increase delivered within seven years.

The £2bn a year cost would be funded through savings in other areas, including cutting the aid budget by £1bn and reducing the budget of the Department for Culture Media and Sport by £1bn.

The Labour government has promised to add 14,000 extra prison space by 2031.

The Tories argued increasing prison places would cut crime and prevent reoffending by keeping serious criminals off the streets.

Shadow justice secretary Nick Timothy said: "Prison works. It works by punishing and deterring, but most importantly by incapacitating.

"Prison should keep violent and repeat offenders away from the law-abiding public."

Tories aim to be election-ready ahead of party conference

The prison population has risen significantly in recent decades, partly as a result of longer sentences and more people being returned to prison for breaching the conditions of their release.

Successive governments have pledged to increase the number of prison places - but delivery has often fallen short of those promises.

New prisons take years to build, often facing local opposition and obstacles in the planning process.

The Prison Governors' Association said: "Building 50,000 cells is one thing; finding the thousands of experienced officers, governors and specialists needed to run them safely is quite another.

"Politicians have spent years announcing prison places while the service struggles with overcrowding, ageing infrastructure and staffing shortages. The real test is not how many places can be promised, but how many prisons can be operated safely, effectively, and sustainably."
